content:
Key observations:
- Corn leaf, close-up view
- Small, circular to oval spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Spots have tan/light brown centers with what appear to be darker (brownish to purplish) rings and yellow halos around some
- The spots are relatively small — roughly pencil-eraser sized or smaller
- A few tiny black dots visible near the midrib area
- No elongated cigar-shaped lesions (rules out Northern Leaf Blight)
- No rectangular vein-bounded lesions (rules out Gray Leaf Spot)
- No rust pustules (rules out Common Rust/Southern Rust)
- No large tar spot stromata

The small circular spots with tan centers, darker rings, and yellow halos match **Eyespot** very well. Eyespot lesions are described as small circular water-soaked spots that develop into tan spots surrounded by brown to purple rings with narrow yellow halos — exactly matching what's visible here.

Holcus Spot is also possible (circular tan spots with reddish margins and yellow halos), but Holcus spots are typically larger (1/8 to 1/4 inch) and described as papery-textured with irregular shapes. The pattern here — many small, uniformly circular spots with the characteristic concentric ring/halo — is more consistent with Eyespot.
